evidence.excerpt: The COVID-19 pandemic produced an unprecedented and heterogeneous demand shock in urban hotel markets. Using daily administrative revenue data from 31 hotels in Belgrade, Novi Sad, Kragujevac, and Niš for the period January 2019 to December 2022, this paper estimates city-specific demand recovery curves and evaluates whether hotels that adopted aggressive repricing during the trough phase recovered faster than those that maintained pre-pandemic rate levels. A synthetic control method is applied to construct counterfactual recovery paths for each property. Results show that hotels that cut average daily rates by more than 20% during the trough recovered to 90% of pre-pandemic RevPAR roughly 4.2 months earlier on average, but at a cost of sustained brand dilution measurable in online review scores 18 months later. The trade-off between short-run occupancy gains and longer-run reputation effects is quantified and discussed.
